faq.a: Asha is associated with the Arabic form عَائِشَة, whose core sense is asha; living, alive (swahili form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Asha?
faq.a: Asha is associated with Arabic. Asha is the Swahili form of Arabic عَائِشَة (ʿĀʾisha), meaning 'living, alive'.
Yes — the underlying form عَائِشَة is Arabic.
Asha can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Asha should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿĀʾisha is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Asha mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Asha is rendered عائشہ and carries the sense عائشہ، زندہ.

faq.q: What does Asha mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Asha is rendered عایشه and carries the sense عایشه، زنده.
A romanized syllable approximation is as-ha. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Asha?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Asha, asha. Script forms are عائشہ, عايشه, عایشه, عَائِشَة, आइशा.

faq.q: Is Asha a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
